turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Afternoon. Who've we got today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Oliver, ten days old. We came because his skin's gone yellow.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Where's the yellow?

[SEG0005] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Face and chest, and the whites of his eyes. My sister noticed when she brought a lasagne round, lovely of her, but it's the colour that got us in. I don't reckon it's on his legs.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did it start?

[SEG0007] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Um he feeds every four hours. Breast first, then a top-up, we began that on day four 'cause he was dozy on the breast and the midwife said a little formula was alright, Aptamil Gold, and he...
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): The yellow. When?
[SEG0009] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, sorry. Four days ago. Eyes first, then the skin, so about day six.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0011] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. No fever at all. He's warm like a normal bub, I didn't even get the thermometer out of the drawer.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Vomiting?
[SEG0013] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No vomiting. He does a bit of posset after a feed, milky, not much, just on the wrap.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Pale stools?
[SEG0015] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Mustard yellow and seedy. I check every nappy, bit obsessive I know, there's a note on the fridge.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Dark wee?
[SEG0017] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No, wee looks pale. Six wet nappies yesterday, I counted them.
[SEG0018] person_1 (DOCTOR): What did he weigh?
[SEG0019] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Nurse read three point four eight kilograms. Birth weight was three point six two, so he's nearly back up, which settled me a bit.
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): Mmm.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Breast and bottle?

[SEG0022] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Both, yeah. I breastfeed and his dad gives sixty mils of the Aptamil every four hours. Overnight it went to five hours once. Sometimes he leaves about twenty mils in the bottle.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sleepy to feed?
[SEG0024] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was sleepy those first few days. Not now. He wakes himself and cries for it, quite cross actually, little fists going.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any breathing problems?
[SEG0026] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No. Breathing's easy, I sit and watch him sometimes when he sleeps just to be sure, but it's been fine.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yellow to the chest, legs clear. Fontanelle's soft. Belly soft, no liver edge. Not dry.
[SEG0028] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): No liver edge, ok. I googled biliary atresia at two in the morning, terrible idea, and then I was awake till the birds started, his dad told me off.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Prolonged jaundice. Most likely breast milk jaundice. Can't rule out a conjugated problem until the bloods.
[SEG0030] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Right. So what do we actually do? I brought spare nappies and a bottle, the car park meter only does two hours which is annoying.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Bloods today. Total and conjugated bilirubin. Nurse will take it this afternoon before you leave. Feed as usual, don't fast him.
[SEG0032] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): This arvo, ok. Will he scream? The newborn heel prick was awful, I nearly cried more than he did.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Quick heel prick. I'll see you in two days with the number.

[SEG0034] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two days, so Thursday? Do we just turn up? And mum reckons I should drop the formula because she says it makes babies more yellow, she was very firm on the phone last night, but I don't want him hungry.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thursday, here. Keep the breast and the formula. If the conjugated bilirubin is raised, we book an ultrasound.
[SEG0036] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if the number's sort of in the middle?
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the total is only borderline, we repeat the blood test in a week. Not booking that today.
[SEG0038] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A week, got it. Will someone ring me if it's properly high? I check the phone every ten minutes, took it in the shower yesterday, ridiculous.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll ring if it's high. Otherwise just Thursday.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Ah ah.
[SEG0041] person_2 (FAMILY_MEMBER): That's a hunger noise, he's due. What if he goes floppy or stops wetting, do I wait?
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): If he's floppy, won't feed, or the yellow races down the legs, come straight in. Don't wait till Thursday.

spec.situation: Parents with a ten-day-old baby, yellow skin and feeding every four hours; weight read by the nurse; breast milk plus formula; blood test for bilirubin planned today.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

bad.reason: Doctor states prolonged jaundice, most likely breast milk jaundice; basis about chest jaundice, age, feeding is not explicitly stated.
bad.text: Prolonged jaundice, most likely breast milk jaundice (certainty=provisional, basis=Jaundice to the chest at ten days while still feeding, stated_by=doctor)

omissions.text: Feeding details omitted: breast first, then formula top-up was started on day 4 because he was dozy on the breast, per midwife advice.
Sometimes feeds stretch to every 5 hours overnight only once; otherwise feeds every 4 hours.
Wet nappies quantified as six yesterday.
Stools described as mustard yellow and seedy.
Sleepiness to feed is currently denied: he is not sleepy now, wakes himself and cries for feeds.
Follow-up timing/location clarified as Thursday here.
Planned blood sample method was a heel prick.
